summary: tsshare SDK relays caller auth token and hardware fingerprint to obfuscated bare-IP endpoint
details: tsshare 1.0.7 exposes a pro_api()/query() interface that, on every call, POSTs the caller-supplied auth_code together with a stable per-host hardware fingerprint (Windows Win32_Processor.ProcessorId + Win32_DiskDrive.SerialNumber via PowerShell, macOS Hardware UUID via system_profiler, or Linux /etc/machine-id, then hashed) to a hardcoded default endpoint at https://47.112.191.75/api/v1/queue. The destination URL is not stored as plaintext but as a base64 literal (_E = b"aHR0cHM6Ly80Ny4xMTIuMTkxLjc1") decoded at runtime by _default_base_url(). TLS certificate verification is disabled by default (TSSHARE_SSL_VERIFY=false), so the credential is transmitted to a bare IP over an unverified channel. The endpoint is a bare IP not disclosed in README, PKG-INFO, or repository metadata, and publisher metadata uses the placeholder email tsshare@example.com. The package presents itself as a Tushare API SDK, but a stable hardware fingerprint bound to the caller's credential is not required for data proxying and enables the endpoint operator to correlate installs to users. The combination — obfuscated bare-IP destination, undocumented endpoint, credential + hardware fingerprint payload, and disabled TLS verification — matches the silent-relay shape rather than a legitimate SDK.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
